transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Well, uh... I guess work sent me. I've been missing things. Just... forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, stuff like that. Even basic follow-ups I told people I'd do. It's just piled up, and... yeah, they said I needed to come here before I lose my chance at a promotion. So, here I am.
Have you had trouble with focus or remembering tasks like this before, or has this mainly started recently?

No, it's... it's not new. I guess I've always been this way. 

Even back in grade school, long before this job. Teachers used to say I was bright, but... I was always misplacing my papers. Or I'd just miss parts of the directions. They always had to remind me to actually finish my classwork. So... yeah. It's not just recently.
Do you also find yourself forgetting things or having trouble staying focused in other parts of your life, like at home or when running errands?

Uh... I don't really know. I haven't... I haven't really paid much attention to that. Mostly I just try to get through my shifts. Home is just... I don't really keep track of things there, so I'm not sure.

Can you think of times at home or when you're not at work — like when you're running errands or doing chores — where you've forgotten things you meant to do or had trouble focusing on what you were doing?

I... I really couldn't give you a specific example. Like I said, I don't pay much attention to that stuff. 

Chores are just chores. If I don't get to something around the house, or... if I forget to grab something at the store, it just waits. I don't really think about it.

So you mentioned that you've had these issues at work and even back in grade school, but do you also notice them in other places, like when you're out with friends, doing personal projects, or even just trying to follow a conversation?

I don't know. I guess I don't really do much outside of work. I don't have a lot of personal projects going on. And with friends... I don't know, we just hang out. I haven't really noticed if I miss things they say. It's just normal, I guess.
Do you ever notice yourself losing focus or forgetting things during social activities, like when you're out with friends or trying to follow a conversation?

I... I don't really know. Like I said, I just... I don't pay much attention to that kind of thing. When I'm with people, I'm just there. If I drift off, nobody really says anything, so... I couldn't tell you.
Do you ever have trouble focusing or remembering things when you're doing something for fun or when you're by yourself?
I don't really know. When I'm by myself... I just do whatever. I don't really keep track of if I'm focusing or not. It's just my time, so it doesn't really matter.
Can you tell me if you often lose focus or forget things even when you're doing something you enjoy, like watching a movie, reading, or playing a game?

I guess... I mean, mostly I notice it at work. Like, if I have to pull up a work order on the tablet. I'll start looking at it, thinking I know what I'm supposed to fix. But then... I don't know, maybe somebody drops a wrench or a machine starts up, and my mind just goes to that instead. Next thing I know, I'm staring at the screen and I have no idea what I just read. I don't really read or watch movies much at home, so... that's just how it is on the job.
When you're by yourself at home, doing something you enjoy like scrolling on your phone or watching a show, do you find yourself losing focus or forgetting what you were doing?
I... I don't really know. Like I said, I don't really watch shows. If I'm on my phone, I'm just looking at it. I don't really pay attention to whether I'm focused or not. It's just... what I do.
When you're by yourself at home, maybe scrolling on your phone or doing something on the computer, do you catch yourself losing track of time or not remembering what you were just looking at?
I don't know... I guess time just passes. I don't really sit there trying to remember what I just scrolled past. Once I'm off the clock, I just... let my brain rest. So, I couldn't really tell you.

When you're at home or in other non-work settings, do you find yourself getting distracted easily or having trouble keeping your focus on what you're doing, even if it's something simple like reading instructions or following a conversation?

I... I'm not really sure. Like I said, I don't really pay attention to that stuff when I'm at home. If I'm talking to someone... I don't know, I guess I hear them fine. I just don't really think about it.
When you're by yourself at home, maybe scrolling on your phone or doing something on the computer, do you catch yourself forgetting why you opened an app or losing track of what you were doing?
I mean... sometimes, maybe? I don't really keep track of why I open an app. I just open it. If I forget, I just close it again. It's not really something I think about.

When you're at home, do you ever try to focus on something like following a recipe, reading something online, or figuring out instructions for something, and find that you lose focus or can't keep track of what you're doing?

I don't really do recipes... I guess I notice it more with work stuff. Like... if I pull up a digital work order. I'll start reading the notes, thinking I've got it figured out, but... halfway through, my mind just kind of slips off. I'll hear a noise in the building or start thinking about the next job... and then I realize I don't even know what I just looked at. So... yeah. I guess so.
Can you think of a time in the last week when you were at home or out with friends and realized you had forgotten something important or lost focus on what you were doing, even for a short while?

I... no. Not really. I don't go out much anyway. And at home... I don't know. If I forget something, I just forget it. I don't really sit around keeping a list of it. So... no, nothing specific comes to mind.

Can you think of any examples from the past week, even small ones, where you were in a social setting or doing something for yourself and realized you had completely forgotten what you were supposed to be doing or lost track of the conversation?

I... I think I just said, I don't really go out much. So, no. And if I'm just doing my own thing... I don't know. If I lose track of something, I probably don't even realize I did it in the first place. So I can't really give you an example from this week.

Can you tell me if you’ve noticed any times in the past week, even small ones, when you were at home or interacting with someone — maybe even just a quick conversation — where you realized you had completely lost focus or couldn’t remember what you were doing or supposed to do?

I feel like we're just going in circles here. I... I don't know what else to tell you. I already said I can't think of anything like that from this week. If I'm talking to someone, I guess I'm just talking to them. I'm not... tracking my focus. So, no.
Can you tell me if you often lose focus or forget things even when you're doing something you enjoy, like watching a movie, reading, or playing a game?

I don't really read much. And with movies or TV... if it's on, it's just on. I'm usually just tired after work. If I miss a scene or something, I miss it. It's not something I really pay attention to. So... no, I guess not.

When you're at home and trying to do something that takes a little more thinking, like figuring out a problem on your phone or reading something online, do you find yourself getting distracted or forgetting what you were doing?
I... I don't really know. If I'm on my phone, I'm just scrolling or whatever. I'm not really paying attention to whether I'm getting distracted. It's just... something to do. So, I don't think so.
Can you tell me if you often lose focus or forget things even when you're doing something you enjoy, like watching a movie, reading, or playing a game?
You... you just asked me that. About the movies and stuff. Like I said, I don't really pay attention to that kind of thing. I just watch whatever's on. I don't know what else to say about it.
When you're at home watching something on TV or playing a game, do you ever catch yourself not remembering what just happened or losing track of the story or gameplay?

I... I don't really know why we're going in circles here. Like I said, I'm just tired. I watch TV to zone out, not to memorize it. If I forget a part, it doesn't matter. I just... I don't really keep track of that stuff.

This supports a diagnosis of F48.0 (Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder). Other conditions like F06.7 (Personality change due to a general medical condition), F33.0 (Recurrent depressive disorder, current mild episode), F43.20 (Adjustment disorder without disturbance of conduct), and F07.81 (Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive type, unspecified) have been ruled out or subsumed under the more specific and encompassing diagnosis of F48.0.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking psychiatric evaluation
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent pattern of inattention and forgetfulness that has been present since childhood, confirmed by both current and historical reports. Symptoms are most prominent in structured environments (e.g., work, school), but the patient is either unaware or non-specific about manifestations in non-structured settings. The chronic and early-onset nature of the symptoms, in the absence of clear mood or psychotic features, supports the diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation.
